stable.label: iOS 27
stable.notes: Major release introducing Siri AI (the next generation of Apple Intelligence), improved performance (faster app launches, Photos loading, and AirDrop), powerful parental controls, and an expansive set of software improvements. Available on iPhone 11 and later. Some features (including full Siri AI) are chip-gated to newer models.

upcomingFeature.label: iOS 27.1
upcomingFeature.notes: Estimated feature update — expected to expand Siri AI language support (French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese, Spanish), additional Apple Cash features, RCS business messaging, and further refinements. Date is a community estimate, not confirmed by Apple — check Settings > General > Software Update for the actual release.

beta.label: iOS 27.2 (beta)
beta.notes: Developer beta already in testing. Contains early work on the release after 27.1. Not recommended on a primary device.

communitySentiment.label: Generally positive after launch week
communitySentiment.summary: iOS 27 launched on September 14 with the expected major-version teething issues reported in the first few days (intermittent Wi-Fi drops, Bluetooth pairing hiccups with AirPods/CarPlay, and occasional Face ID false rejections on the newest Pro models). Most of those reports subsided quickly. A temporary battery dip for 24–48 hours after any major update is normal while the system reindexes Spotlight and Photos — it is not itself a sign of a bad update. Overall reception of Siri AI and the performance improvements has been positive on supported hardware.
communitySentiment.sourceNote: Compiled by hand from public reporting (Apple Newsroom, developer release notes, MacRumors forums, tech press). Not a live feed — refresh this file's data manually after checking current reports, or wire in a real backend if you want continuous monitoring.

pointReleaseAdvice: Major .0 releases carry the highest early risk. Point releases (x.0.1, x.1) bring bug and security fixes with lower risk — install those as they appear. If you're not in a hurry and your device is older, waiting a week or two after a major launch is a reasonable way to skip the roughest days.
